claim: LoopError docstring says a run ends with it 'when a frame throws, whatever it throws', that the throw leaves the simulation errored, and that exception is a wrapper whose cause is the raw error; a fault outside the frame ends stopped and holds the raw exception (run! docstring, sim.jl:1514, repeats it)
fix: LoopError: "A run ends with it when the loop fails. A throw inside a [frame](@ref g-frame), whatever it throws, leaves the simulation `errored`, and the previous [snapshot](@ref g-snapshot) is the run's final one. A fault outside the frame, such as `frame!`'s refusal of a frame past the last the run may take, leaves it `stopped` at its last settled boundary. … `exception` holds the failure as the loop caught it. From inside a frame it is a wrapper whose `cause` is the raw error or the failed check's diagnostic, beside the time and the place in the frame where it was thrown. From outside the frame it is the raw exception." run!: "A failure inside a frame leaves the simulation `errored` instead, the cause kept on the record, and a fault outside the frame leaves it `stopped` with the same record. With no device rostered, `run!` then rethrows the failure."
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:1749-1758 builds LoopError(cause) for any loop fault. A fault outside the frame leaves the model consistent, and the run reads stopped. Probe probe.jl:71-72 runs an unbounded run! on test_lattices' long-period rig: it throws ArgumentInvalid(:frame!, :range, k = 1001) and ends lifecycle :stopped with LoopError whose exception is the raw DiagnosticError{ArgumentInvalid}, not a StepError wrapper (also test/test_lattices.jl:404-408). The LoopError docstring (sim.jl:100-108) says a run ends with it when a frame throws, that this leaves the simulation errored, and that exception is a wrapper. run!'s docstring (sim.jl:1514) says a failure inside the loop leaves it errored. Spec §13.5 (spec.md:11915-11923) took the out-of-frame case in commit f010ff26 (2026-11-11), after the docstring's commit afc15682 (2026-11-05).

claim: Each advance reads an honoured stop request off the latest snapshot before it reads the pending control stop word; with both holding, the record names ModelRequestedStop, whereas spec §13.5's fixed order puts the control stop first
fix: Spec §13.5: "The sources are consulted in a fixed order. Every advance reads the latest snapshot's requests at its entry, and the loop reads the requests at each publication, ending the run there. A pending control stop and `t_end` are read at the next frame top. A request holding at a boundary therefore names the record ahead of a control stop pending or a `t_end` reached at the same boundary." The alternative is a code change: read the stop word and t_end ahead of `_stop_hit` at entry and at each frame-ending publication.
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:2090-2091 reads `_stop_hit` and returns ModelRequestedStop before the loop reads `control.stop_issuer` (2099-2100). Inside the loop, a request read at a publication (2115, 2141) returns before the next frame top's control and t_end checks. Probe probe.jl:100 does stop!(sim) and then step! with a request holding at boundary zero: the record is ModelRequestedStop, and with requests ignored (probe.jl:103) the same pending word gives ControlRequestedStop(:code). probe.jl:106 sets t_end = 0.3 with a request holding at the 0.3 publication: the record at t = 0.3 is ModelRequestedStop, and without the request (probe.jl:108) it is EndTimeReached. Spec §13.5 (spec.md:11858-11861) and D-203 (log.md:8101-8103) fix the order as control stop, then t_end, then requests, the first naming the record when two hold at one boundary. D-413 rules the entry read itself, but not its precedence over the control stop.
